tasks.title: Produce implementation plan for a string utilities module
tasks.prompt:
You are the PLANNING agent in a multi-agent pipeline. Work only inside your current workspace directory.

Create a file named exactly PLAN.md containing an implementation plan for a small, pure-Python string-utilities module. Requirements the plan must cover:

1. A module named stringutils.py exposing these pure functions:
   - slugify(text: str) -> str  (lowercase, non-alphanumerics collapsed to single hyphen, stripped hyphens at both ends)
   - camel_to_snake(text: str) -> str
   - truncate(text: str, max_len: int) -> str  (append '...' when truncated; max_len includes the ellipsis; raise ValueError if max_len < 4)
   - is_palindrome(text: str) -> bool  (case-insensitive, ignores non-alphanumeric characters)
2. A unittest test module named test_stringutils.py covering normal cases, edge cases, and the ValueError path.
3. Every rule the tests must assert (be specific).
4. Acceptance criteria as a checklist.

MANDATORY: the first line of PLAN.md must be exactly:
{marker_line}

Do not create any other files. Do not run any commands other than reading/writing files. When done, reply with just: PLAN-COMPLETE

tasks.title: Implement stringutils module + tests from the approved plan
tasks.prompt:
You are the BACKEND IMPLEMENTATION agent in a multi-agent pipeline. Work only inside your current workspace directory.

A planning agent produced the following plan. Implement it EXACTLY as specified.

===== BEGIN PLAN (verbatim from planner) =====
{plan_text}
===== END PLAN =====

Rules:
- Create stringutils.py and test_stringutils.py implementing every function and every asserted rule in the plan.
- The first line of the stringutils.py module docstring must be exactly:
{marker_line}
- Run the tests yourself with: python3 -m unittest discover -v
- Iterate until all tests pass. Do not modify the tests to make failing code pass unless the plan itself is internally contradictory (if so, note it in your final reply).
- Do not create any other files.
When done, reply with the final unittest summary line (e.g. 'OK') and nothing else.

tasks.title: Build standalone demo page for the planned string utilities
tasks.prompt:
You are the FRONTEND IMPLEMENTATION agent in a multi-agent pipeline. Work only inside your current workspace directory.

A planning agent produced this plan for a Python string-utilities module:

===== BEGIN PLAN (verbatim from planner) =====
{plan_text}
===== END PLAN =====

Create a single-file interactive demo page named exactly index.html that:
- Is valid standalone HTML (doctype, <html>...</html>, embedded <style> and <script>, no external assets, no CDNs).
- Re-implements the four planned functions (slugify, camel_to_snake, truncate with the same ValueError-equivalent guard, is_palindrome with the same ignore-rules) in plain JavaScript, mirroring the planned Python semantics exactly.
- Provides a text input, a function selector (radio or select for the four functions), a numeric field for truncate's max_len, a Run button, and an output area.
- Shows an inline error message (not a crash) when truncate is given max_len < 4.
- Contains an HTML comment on line 2 with exactly this text: {marker_line}
- Looks clean with simple CSS (dark text on light background, readable spacing). No frameworks.
Do not create any other files. When done, reply with just: FRONTEND-COMPLETE

tasks.title: Independent review of implementation, frontend, and verification results
tasks.prompt:
You are the INDEPENDENT REVIEW agent. You did not write any of this code. Judge it strictly.

A planner, a backend implementer, and a frontend implementer produced the following. A deterministic verifier already ran the backend tests OUTSIDE any LLM; its result is reported below and you must treat it as ground truth for test pass/fail (you may critique test quality regardless).

===== VERIFICATION RESULT (ground truth, produced by deterministic verifier) =====
{verify_summary}
===== END VERIFICATION RESULT =====

===== PLAN (verbatim) =====
{plan_text}
===== END PLAN =====

===== backend/stringutils.py =====
```python
{implement_stringutils}
```

===== backend/test_stringutils.py =====
```python
{implement_test_stringutils}
```

===== frontend/index.html =====
```html
{frontend_index}
```

Write a file named exactly REVIEW.md assessing:
1. Plan compliance: does the implementation match every planned function/rule?
2. Test quality: do the tests actually pin the planned behavior (edge cases, error path)?
3. Frontend fidelity: does the JS mirror the planned semantics (truncate guard, palindrome ignore-rules)?
4. Any bug, security note, or spec deviation.

The file MUST end with exactly one line in this format:
VERDICT: approve|request_changes — <one-sentence justification>

The first line of REVIEW.md must be exactly:
{marker_line}

Do not create any other files. When done, reply with just the VERDICT line.
